lines.trans: What, so we can advertise to everyone that Cindy vanished?
Since I could not go to the police for security footage, I apologetically tailed you instead, Producer.
I even saw Cindy walk right out of that building and sort all the recyclables.
Why could that girl not just sit still inside—sorting recyclables while supposedly in hiding!
She turned out so different from how she looks—spotlessly neat.
It was dark so I could not see and swung with all my strength—are you okay?
Please let it slide just for tonight—it is her birthday.
It is because CEO Byun's mood is ominous right now—you know what kind of person she is.
I understand, so just head back tonight—I take full responsibility for bringing Cindy home, and fireworks start any minute.

meanings.note: Basic verb of motion. With the respectful ending -세요 in 안녕히 가세요, it forms the polite farewell 'Goodbye!'. RR: gada.

examples.trans: I am going home.
Go safely!

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (adv).

examples.text: 가만히 있는 사람 아주 심란하게 흔들어 놓고, 연애하고 선 보고 소개팅하고!
examples.trans: You shook up someone who was minding her own business, and now you date, do matchmaking meetings, and go on blind dates!
Here the word for 'quietly, minding one's business' is key.

meanings.note: Colloquial contraction of 그 아이 ('that child/kid'); used only for younger people or close peers.

examples.trans: Are you close with her?
He is late every day.

related.gloss: this kid / he or she (near speaker)
that kid / he or she (over there)

meanings.note: Bound noun often contracted to 거 in everyday speech.

examples.trans: This is my bag.
Because I think I'm late.
Did you hear about this police station?
I was busy today because of police station.

meanings.note: Honorific equivalent of 있다; used in 안녕히 계세요 ('goodbye' to someone staying).

examples.trans: Goodbye! (to someone staying)
Is the teacher inside right now?

meanings.note: Indicates that something will happen in a very short time.

examples.trans: The bus will arrive soon.
I will contact you again soon.

meanings.note: Used as purposive -게 question (광고하게?!).

examples.trans: What, so we can advertise to the whole world that Cindy vanished?!

examples.text: 우리 엄마는 영화배우 장국영 좋아했는데 아빠가 장국영이 광고하는 초콜릿 백 개씩 사다 바쳐야 엄마랑 사귈 수 있었대요.
examples.trans: My mom loved actor Leslie Cheung, and she said my dad had to bring her a hundred chocolates from his commercials just to date her.

괜찮다.gloss: to be fine; to be okay

meanings.en: to be fine; to be okay; to be alright
meanings.note: Used to reassure someone, decline an offer politely, or say something is acceptable.

examples.trans: I'm really fine.
Is it okay if we meet tomorrow?

meanings.note: refers to something known to both speakers or near the listener

examples.trans: That movie was really fun.
What is that person's name?

meanings.note: Softens a statement or downplays a motive.

examples.trans: I just asked out of curiosity.
I'll just stay home today.

그러다.gloss: to say so; to do so

meanings.en: to say so; to speak like that
meanings.note: contracted from 그러하다; often follows quoted speech

meanings.en: to do so; to act like that

examples.trans: Who said that?
That friend also said they are going together.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (adj).

examples.text: 설령 조금 취했다 해도 술버릇이 굉장히 깔끔한 편이라.
examples.trans: Even supposing I do get slightly tipsy, my drinking habits are remarkably neat.
This expression comes from 'clean, neat'.

meanings.note: Plain first-person singular pronoun used with friends, younger people, or subordinates; contracts to 난 with -는 and becomes 내가 before -가.

examples.trans: I'm going to stay home today.
I'll go first.

meanings.en: to appear, be published, be achieved (a score/result)
meanings.note: Used for ratings, test scores, or results coming out

examples.trans: I came outside from the house.
The exam results came out well.

meanings.note: Used colloquially for positive or negative emphasis.
Original sense of exceeding a limit.

examples.trans: The weather is so nice today.
Don't worry too much.

meanings.note: Placed before the verb it modifies.

examples.trans: I finished all my homework.
I ate all the rice.

meanings.note: 르-irregular adjective; conjugates as 달라요 in polite present.
In its adnominal form 다른, modifies a following noun to mean 'other' or 'another'.

examples.trans: Do you have any other questions?
Our thoughts are different from each other.

meanings.note: Used as sequential -해서 (다해서).

examples.text: 내가 어두워서 안 보여서 있는 힘을 다해서 세게 쳤는데 괜찮으셔?
examples.trans: It was dark so I could not see and swung with all my strength—are you okay?
Let us do that (using all and) right away.
He is our company's president.
I will speak as the representative.

meanings.note: Used as promissive -ㄹ게 (데려다줄게.).

examples.text: 아니 돈도 없다면서, 아우 참 대책 없네! 집이 어디예요, 우리가 데려다줄게.
examples.trans: Wait, you say you have no money either—talk about zero plan! Where is your home? We will drop you off.
Let us do that (will give you a ride) right away.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 그래서 요 며칠 내 뒤를 졸졸 따라다니면서 선배를 떠봐?
examples.trans: So that is why you trailed behind me like a puppy these past few days sounding out your senior?
Here the word for 'behind me' is key.

meanings.note: Placed before a verb to express inability or impossibility.

examples.text: 어제는 너무 피곤해서 잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.trans: I was so tired yesterday that I couldn't sleep.
Because it rained, we couldn't go on the picnic.

meanings.note: Placed directly before a noun in questions

examples.trans: What kind of music are you listening to right now?
Is something the matter?

meanings.note: Used as idiomatic formal past (밟았습니다.).

examples.text: 경찰서에 신고할 수가 없어서 CCTV는 확인을 못 했고요, 너무 죄송하게도 피디님 뒤를 제가 좀 밟았습니다.
examples.trans: Since I could not go to the police for security footage, I apologetically tailed you instead, Producer.
Let us do that (tailed, shadowed) right away.

meanings.note: Used as noun + comitative + topic (보기랑은).

examples.text: 보기랑은 참 다르더라고요, 아주 그냥 깔끔하고.
examples.trans: She turned out so different from how she looks—spotlessly neat.
This point about from appearances is really important.

보다.gloss: to see, to watch; to take (an exam)

meanings.en: to see, to look at, to watch
meanings.note: Primary meaning.
Idiomatic in 시험을 보다.

examples.trans: I watched a movie on the weekend.
I took the driver's license exam.
I want to is it visible? right now.
How about trying to is it visible? together tomorrow?
I want to even if looking out for right now.
How about trying to even if looking out for together tomorrow?

meanings.note: Honorific noun and counter for people, used instead of 사람.

examples.trans: That person over there is our teacher.
How many people are in your party?

meanings.note: Used as compound noun + -도 (분리수거도).

examples.text: 전혀요, 집에 정리할 게 너무 많아서 분리수거도 하고 낮잠도 자고요.
examples.trans: Not at all—there was so much to tidy around the house that I sorted the recycling and took a nap too.
This point about recycling sorting too is really important.

meanings.note: Used as connective -고 (분리수거하고).

examples.text: 신디가 그 집에서 나와가지고 분리수거하고 그러는 것도 제가 다 봤거든요.
examples.trans: I even saw Cindy walk right out of that building and sort all the recyclables.
Let us do that (sorting recyclables and) right away.

meanings.note: Used as compound noun (불꽃놀이).

examples.trans: They say fireworks are one hour away—hurry over!

examples.text: 아이고, 얘는 온다 온다 하고 왜 이렇게 안 와? 불꽃놀이 그렇게 좋아하면서 20분밖에 안 남았구먼!
examples.trans: Good grief, she keeps saying she is coming—why is she still not here when fireworks start in twenty minutes?!

meanings.note: Used as prospective adnominal (사라질).

examples.text: 말 같지도 않은 걸 뭘 신경 써요? 오늘부터 활동 시작하면 싹 사라질 겁니다.
examples.trans: Why bother over nonsense? Once I resume promotions starting today, it will all vanish.

examples.text: 그게 분명히 차에 태워서 출발을 했는데 운전하다가 돌아보니까 사라져 있더래요.
examples.trans: Well, he swears he put her in the van and pulled out, yet when he looked back while driving she had vanished.

meanings.note: Used as noun + exclamatory copula (생일이네!).

examples.trans: Really? Today is your birthday! Happy day you were born!

examples.text: 그걸 내가 알았니? 준모야, 우리 저녁에 신디 생일 파티 해주자!
examples.trans: How was I supposed to know?! Joon-mo, let us throw Cindy a birthday party tonight!
It really is strongly, boldly compared to what I thought.
Especially today, it is strongly, boldly and nice.

meanings.note: Bound noun used in -(으)ㄹ 수 있다/없다 ('can / cannot').

examples.trans: I can read Korean.
I cannot go today.

meanings.note: used both transitively and intransitively

examples.trans: The meeting is starting soon.
I started studying Korean.

meanings.note: Used as prospective adnominal (신고할).

examples.text: 경찰서에 신고할 수가 없어서 CCTV는 확인을 못 했고요, 너무 죄송하게도 피디님 뒤를 제가 좀 밟았습니다.
examples.trans: Since I could not go to the police for security footage, I apologetically tailed you instead, Producer.
Let us do that (report) right away.

meanings.note: Used as idiomatic stem + -가 (심상치가).

examples.text: 변 대표님이 심상치가 않아서 그래요. 아시잖아요, 어떤 분이신지.
examples.trans: It is because CEO Byun's mood is ominous right now—you know what kind of person she is.
I thought it over again (unusual, ominous).

meanings.note: Used as acronym noun + topic (CCTV는).

examples.text: 경찰서에 신고할 수가 없어서 CCTV는 확인을 못 했고요, 너무 죄송하게도 피디님 뒤를 제가 좀 밟았습니다.
examples.trans: Since I could not go to the police for security footage, I apologetically tailed you instead, Producer.
This point about security cameras is really important.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (adv).

examples.text: 변 대표랑 준모랑 서로 쌍소리 오가고 촬영장 아주 개판 됐대요.
examples.trans: They say CEO Byun and Joon-mo traded harsh words and the set turned into a total mess.
Here the word for 'completely' is key.

meanings.note: Short-form negation placed directly before verbs and adjectives

examples.trans: I'm not going to the office today.
I haven't watched that movie yet.

meanings.note: Used in standard farewells 안녕히 계세요 and 안녕히 가세요.

examples.trans: Goodbye! (to someone staying)
Goodbye! (to someone leaving)

않다.gloss: to not do, to not be

meanings.en: to not do, to not be
meanings.note: Auxiliary negative verb/adjective used after -지 (long-form negation)

examples.trans: The weather isn't cold today.
I didn't say anything.

meanings.note: ㄹ-irregular verb: stem 알- drops ㄹ before ㄴ, ㅂ, ㅅ (e.g., 압니까)

examples.trans: Do you know that person's phone number?
Yes, I know well.

meanings.note: Used as causal -어서 (어두워서).

examples.text: 내가 어두워서 안 보여서 있는 힘을 다해서 세게 쳤는데 괜찮으셔?
examples.trans: It was dark so I could not see and swung with all my strength—are you okay?
It is really dark, so compared to what I expected.

meanings.en: to be how, to be in what state
meanings.note: Its adverbial form 어떻게 ('how') is used to ask how something is done or how things turned out.

examples.trans: How do you feel today?
How did the meeting turn out?

없다.gloss: to not exist, to not have

meanings.en: to not exist, to not be present

examples.trans: I don't have time right now.
The tickets are all sold out, so there aren't any.

meanings.note: The present day; often used adverbially without a particle.

examples.trans: The weather is nice today.
What day of the week is it today?

있다.gloss: to exist, to have, to stay

meanings.en: to exist, to be (in a place)
meanings.note: Opposite of 없다.
Marks the possessed item with 이/가.

examples.trans: Do you have time?
Nobody is at home.

related.gloss: to not exist, to not have

examples.trans: Listen closely to what I explain.
I eat Korean food well.

meanings.note: Used as slang noun (잠수).

examples.trans: What does it look like? Have none of you ever gone off the grid before?

examples.text: 아니, 지금 퇴원하다가 잠수를 타는 거야? 근데 왜 이 차를 타?
examples.trans: Wait, you are going into hiding right out of the hospital? Why get into this car, though?

meanings.note: Humble first-person singular pronoun used in polite speech.

examples.trans: I have an induction ceremony.
Follow me.
Please give me some water.
Please wait just a moment.

meanings.note: Contraction of 조금
Respectful, polite adjective used to apologize in workplaces and to strangers. Formal 죄송합니다 is the standard workplace apology. RR: joesonghada.

examples.trans: I am very sorry for being late.
I am sorry for the inconvenience.

meanings.note: Used as pejorative bound noun + -에 (주제에).

examples.text: 아니 걔는 그냥 집에 가만히 있지, 무슨 잠수 탄 주제에 분리수거를 하고 그래!
examples.trans: Why could that girl not just sit still inside—sorting recyclables while supposedly in hiding!
This point about for someone who is is really important.
I'm on my way home right now.
On weekends I usually rest at home.

meanings.note: used to emphasize an adjective or adverb

examples.trans: The food is really delicious today.
Time really flies.
If viewers criticize me, are you going to take responsibility, producer?

examples.text: 이번 일은 꼭 잘 해결해 봐요, 책임지다는 마음으로요.
examples.trans: Let's make sure we handle this well (take responsibility).

meanings.en: to hit, to strike, to cause (trouble)
meanings.note: Used in idioms like 사고를 치다 (to cause trouble).

examples.trans: I caused trouble.
I caused trouble. (2)

meanings.note: intransitive verb; also means 'to ride' in another sense

examples.text: 불을 줄이지 않으면 고기가 다 타요.
examples.trans: If you don't lower the heat, the meat will burn completely.
Firewood is burning brightly in the stove.

meanings.note: Hangul spelling of the English abbreviation PD, widely used in Korean broadcasting.

examples.trans: Who is the PD in charge of the new program?

examples.text: 그녀는 예능 피디가 되기 위해 시험을 준비했다.
examples.trans: She prepared for the exam to become a variety PD.

meanings.en: to do, to perform, to hold
meanings.note: Core verb; also combines with nouns to form verbs.

examples.trans: What are you doing right now?
We are holding a meeting today.

examples.text: 게임을 하기 전에 미리 확인을 받으라고? 지금 장난해?
examples.trans: Get approval in advance before every game? Are you kidding me right now?
The topic of confirmation, approval came up during this shoot.

examples.text: 잊지 않고 꼭 갚아 줄 수 있어야 피디한테 힘이 생겨.
examples.trans: Only when people know you remember and repay every debt does a producer gain power.
The topic of power, leverage came up during this shoot.
